# The Art of the Short with Lakshmi Ganapathi: FICO, DoorDash, and AeroVironment

First listed: 2026-09-02 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: The Art of the Short with Lakshmi Ganapathi: FICO, DoorDash, and AeroVironment](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-art-of-the-short-with-lakshmi) - 2026-09-02

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Ganapathi presents shorts in FICO, AeroVironment and DoorDash. Eisman remains short FICO, accepts its competitive threat, and finds the delivery credit-risk argument compelling. Primary evidence supports FICO debt-funded repurchases and expanding VantageScore adoption. It contradicts the asserted national BNPL prevalence and the categorical claim that AeroVironment has been priced out of its market. Numerous valuation, legal and product-comparison premises remain unverified; general BNPL statistics do not establish DoorDash customer exposure.

The most substantiated thesis is erosion of FICO exclusivity and increased leverage. DoorDash and AeroVironment theses rely on unverified exposure, customer economics and product equivalence. Eisman explicitly adopts several claims in the close, while his position disclosures remain distinct from price targets.

## Framework and tools

- Classify shorts by structural competition, product economics and credit exposure.
- Separate poor contractor economics from company profitability.
- Look beyond filings to product quality, warranties and management behavior.
- Monitor debt-funded buybacks and acquisition accounting.
- Require matching denominators before inferring customer dependence.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- FICO mortgage score prices and market share
- Credit-invisible and thin-file population estimates
- Debt and share repurchases
- Switchblade all-up-round budget prices
- Goodwill as a share of assets and impairment charges
- European worker litigation
- BNPL adoption and grocery or delivery use
- Monthly securitization share estimates
